Rashi on Nedarim 58a:1:1.hebrew: כגון טבל - שיש לו מתירין, שמתקנו וניתר; ומעשר והקדש יש לו מתירין על ידי פדייה; וחדש, עומר מתירו. להכי אפילו באלף לא בטלי, דהא אפשר להו בתקנתא:
Rashi on Nedarim 58a:1:1.english: For example, untithed produce [tevel] - For it can become permitted, as one rectifies it [by tithing] and it becomes permitted; and [second] tithe and consecrated items can become permitted through redemption; and [produce of the] new [crop] — the omer [offering] permits it. Therefore, even in [a mixture of] a thousand [times their volume] they are not neutralized, since they can be rectified.

Rashi on Nedarim 58a:1:2.english: The Sages determined a measure for them - For terumah is nullified in one hundred [parts], and orlah in two hundred [parts].

Rashi on Nedarim 58a:2:1.english: The Sabbatical-Year [produce] prohibits [permitted produce] in any amount [when mixed] with its [own] species - For if a se'ah of Sabbatical-Year wheat became mixed into a thousand [se'ah] of permitted [wheat], it is not nullified.

Rashi on Nedarim 58a:2:2.english: He said to them: I too did not say - that Sabbatical-Year [produce] prohibits [produce] of its own species in any amount.

Rashi on Nedarim 58a:2:3.hebrew: אלא לביעור - שאם נטל בצל של ששית ונטעו בשביעית והוסיפה כל שהוא, אותו כל שהוא מבטל את העיקר ומחייב כולו בביעור דמוצאי שביעית:
Rashi on Nedarim 58a:2:3.english: Only with regard to removal - [Meaning] that if one took an onion of the sixth [year] and planted it in the seventh [year], and it grew by any amount, that minute amount nullifies the primary [onion] and obligates all of it in the removal of the conclusion of the seventh [year].

Rashi on Nedarim 58a:3:1.hebrew: אבל לאכילה - שאם נתערבו פירות שביעית בפירות שמינית לאחר שנתחייבו בביעור ולא ביערן, דהשתא קיימי באיסור אכילה, אינה אוסרת אלא בנותן טעם, ואם אין בה בנותן טעם, מתבטל. ומדקתני לא אמרתי אלא לביעור, דגידולין מבטלין את העיקר, התם נמי בבעיא של ישמעאל, גידוליו מבטלין את העיקר:
Rashi on Nedarim 58a:3:1.english: However, [with regard] to eating - For if Sabbatical-Year produce became mixed with eighth-year produce after it became obligated in removal and one did not remove it, such that it now stands under a prohibition of eating, it prohibits [the mixture] only by imparting flavor; and if there is not [enough] in it to impart flavor, it is neutralized. And since [the baraita] teaches, "I said [this] only with regard to removal," [indicating] that growths neutralize the original [item], there too, in the inquiry of Yishmael, its growths neutralize the original [item].

Rashi on Nedarim 58a:3:2.hebrew: הא נמי לחומרא - דהא דאמר לענין ביעור, דגידולין מבטלין את העיקר, היינו נמי לחומרא, שכולן חייבין בביעור — העיקר והתוספת — אבל בעיא דישמעאל להיתר היא:
Rashi on Nedarim 58a:3:2.english: Here too, [it is] a stringency - For that which was stated regarding removal, that the growths nullify the original item, is also a stringency, for all of them are obligated in removal — [both] the original item and the addition — whereas [the] query of [Rabbi] Yishmael is for permissibility.

Rashi on Nedarim 58a:4:1.english: Onions - [Onions] of the sixth [year] upon which rain fell in the seventh [year], and they sprouted on their own without planting.

Rashi on Nedarim 58a:4:2.hebrew: אם היו עלין שלהן שחורין - שמחמת שצמחו יש להן כח עוד ליגדל, אסורין, דודאי גדלי ממי שביעית, וגידוליו מבטלין את העיקר:
Rashi on Nedarim 58a:4:2.english: If their leaves were black - Because they sprouted [and] still have the strength to grow, they are forbidden, for they certainly grew from Sabbatical-Year water, and its [new] growth nullifies the primary [onion].

Rashi on Nedarim 58a:4:3.hebrew: הוריקו - שהן כמו כמושין, ירוקין והכסיפו פניהם — מותרין, שלא גדלו כלום בשביעית:
Rashi on Nedarim 58a:4:3.english: They turned green - [Meaning] that they are as if withered, yellowish-green and their appearance has paled — [they are] permitted, because they did not grow at all during the Sabbatical [year].

Rashi on Nedarim 58a:5:1.hebrew: אם יכולין ליתלש - מן הקרקע בעלין שלהן, שכל כך יש להן כח בעלין שלהן, שכשאוחז בעליהן שומט עיקרו עמו מן הקרקע — אסורין, דחשיבי גידולי שביעית:
Rashi on Nedarim 58a:5:1.english: If they can be uprooted - from the ground by their leaves, [meaning] that they have so much strength in their leaves that when one grasps their leaves, he pulls out its root with it from the ground — they are forbidden, for they are considered Sabbatical-Year growths.

Rashi on Nedarim 58a:5:2.hebrew: כנגדן למוצאי שביעית מותרין - שאם של שביעית, וצמחו בשמינית, ויש להן כח בעלין — מותרין, דגידולי היתר מבטלין העיקר של איסור. והיינו להיתר, כגון הך בעיא דישמעאל, ומהא פשטה:
Rashi on Nedarim 58a:5:2.english: In the parallel [situation], at the conclusion of the Sabbatical Year, they are permitted - That if [they are] of the Sabbatical Year, and they sprouted in the eighth [year], and their leaves have strength [to be uprooted by them], they are permitted, because permitted growths nullify the original forbidden [part]. And this is [a resolution] toward permissibility, like this dilemma of Yishmael, and from this [source] he resolved it.

Rashi on Nedarim 58a:5:3.hebrew: ודלמא - לעולם אין גידולי היתר מבטלין את האיסור, והכא היכי דמי? במדוכנין. כלומר: האי דקתני "וכנגדן למוצאי שביעית מותרין", כגון שהודכו — שכתשן במדוכה — דליתנהו לעיקרן בעינייהו. אבל בבעיא דישמעאל, דאיתיה לעיקר בעין, איכא למימר דלא בטלי:
Rashi on Nedarim 58a:5:3.english: And perhaps - Actually, permitted growth does not nullify the prohibition, and here, what is the case? [It refers] to crushed [onions]. That is to say: this that it teaches, "And in the parallel [situation], at the conclusion of the Sabbatical Year, they are permitted," [is a case] where they were crushed — that one pounded them in a mortar — so that their original [part] is not intact. However, in Yishmael's dilemma, where the original [part] is intact, one can say that they are not nullified.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:1:1.hebrew: כל דבר שיש לו מתירין כגון טבל - שנתערב בחולין, דמצי מעשר עליו מדמאי או מעציץ שאינו נקוב:
Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:1:1.english: Any item that can become permitted, for example, untithed produce [tevel] - that became mixed with non-sacred produce [chullin], for one can separate tithes for it from doubtfully tithed produce [demai] or from [produce grown in] an unperforated pot.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:1:2.english: And second tithe - For it is possible to bring it up [to Jerusalem] and eat it, or to redeem it.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:1:3.english: And new [produce] - for the shining of the east [daybreak] permits [it].

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:1:4.english: And consecrated items - For if he wishes, he can redeem it.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:1:5.hebrew: לא נתנו חכמים שיעור - ואסורין בכל שהוא. ואין להקשות דבפ' בתרא דע"ז (דף עג:) אמר דבטבל שלא במינו בנ"ט, י"ל דהא נמי דאמר שלא נתנו בו שיעור משום דיש לו מתירין — היינו דווקא במינו, אבל שלא במינו בטל; וכן משמע לעיל גבי יין שהוא בנ"ט, ואע"ג דהוי דבר שיש לו מתירין. וא"ת: פרק בתרא דמסכת ע"ז (שם) דקאמר "חוץ מטבל ויין נסך דבמינו במשהו", ופריך: "בשלמא עבודת כוכבים משום חומרא דע"ז, אלא טבל מאי טעמא?", ומסיק: "כהיתרו כך איסורו" — פירוש: דחיטה אחת פוטרת את הכרי — ולימא טעמא משום דיש לו מתירין? וי"ל דהתם בטבל שהלכו בעליו למדינת הים, דאין לו מי יתירו. אבל קשה: למה לי טעם דיש לו מתירין? תיפוק ליה משום דכהיתרו כך איסורו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:1:5.english: The Sages did not determine a measure - And they are forbidden in any minute amount. And one should not raise the difficulty that in the last chapter of Avodah Zarah (73b) it says that tevel [mixed] with a different kind [is prohibited only] by imparting flavor, [for] one can answer that this [statement] too, which says they did not determine a measure for it because it has a means of becoming permitted, applies specifically [when mixed] with its own kind, whereas with a different kind it is nullified; and so it is implied above regarding wine, that it is [prohibited only] by imparting flavor, even though it is something that has a means of becoming permitted. And if you ask [from] the last chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (ibid.), where it says: "Except for tevel and libation wine, which in their own kind [prohibit] in any minute amount," and [the Gemara] asks: "Granted, idolatry [prohibits in any amount] because of the stringency of idolatry; but tevel, what is the reason?" and it concludes: "Like its permitting, so is its prohibition" — meaning, [just as] a single kernel of wheat exempts the [entire] pile — why not say the reason is because it has a means of becoming permitted? One can answer that there [it is speaking] of tevel whose owners went overseas, so it has no one to permit it. However, it is difficult: why do I need the reason of "it has a means of becoming permitted"? Let it be derived from "like its permitting, so is its prohibition"!

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:1:6.english: And any [item] that cannot become permitted, for example, teruma - And later [the Gemara] explains why it is [considered an item that] cannot become permitted.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:1:7.hebrew: וערלה וכלאי הכרם נתנו בו חכמים שיעור - תרומה בק', ערלה וכלאים במאתים; ומיירי במין במינו, דבשאינו מינו אמרי' פ' גיד הנשה (חולין דף צז -) דתרומה בנ"ט:
Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:1:7.english: And orlah and diverse kinds of a vineyard, the Sages gave a measure for it - Terumah [is nullified] in one hundred [parts], orlah and diverse kinds in two hundred; and [this] is speaking of like with like, for with unlike [kinds], we say in the chapter Gid Hanasheh (Chullin 97a) that terumah [is judged] by imparting flavor.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:2:1.hebrew: דתנן השביעית אוסרת בכל שהוא - והא דאיבעי' ליה לעיל אי גידולי דהיתר מבטלין לעיקר דשביעית, י"ל דהכא מיירי בדבר לח, אבל ביבש לא; א"נ שמא גידולי חשיבי טפי ומבטלי עיקר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:2:1.english: As we learned [in a mishna]: "Sabbatical-Year [produce] prohibits in any amount" - And [as for] that which [the Gemara] asked above, whether permitted growths nullify the original root of Sabbatical-Year [produce], one can say that here [the mishna] is speaking of a moist [substance], whereas with a dry [substance, it does] not; or alternatively, perhaps growths are more significant and nullify [the] original root.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:2:2.hebrew: אמר להם שביעית אינה אוסרת בכל שהוא אלא לביעור פירות - פירש הרב רבי אליעזר: כגון פירות ששית שנכנסו בשביעית וגדלו משהו, וצריכין ביעור כפירות שביעית, דגידולי איסור חשיבי ומבטלי לעיקר דהיתר. אבל לאכילה, כגון לאחר ביעור בפירות שביעית שנתערבו בפירות דהיתר — אינו אוסר במשהו, אלא בנותן טעם כשאר איסורין. אלמא דגידולי שביעית מבטלין לעיקר דהיתר; ה"נ נימא בבעיין דבצל דגידולי היתר מבטלי לעיקר דאיסור. ודחי: הא נמי לחומרא אזלינן, דגידולי שביעית מבטלין העיקר, אבל להקל לא מבטלי גידולי דהיתר לעיקר דאיסור. ומה שפירש "אלא לביעור" לענין פירות ששית שנכנסין בשביעית, ק' להר"מ: דתניא, כל הספיחין מותרין חוץ מספיחי כרוב, ומפרשינן דמיירי בספיחי ששית הנכנסים בשביעית — אלמא דגידולי שביעית אינן אוסרין במשהו! ונראה דשמא התם מיירי שגמרו בששית ולא גדלו כלל בשביעית, וספיחי כרוב אסורין כדמפרש: שמא יקח מן העלין ויאמר מן האמהות לקחתי. ועוד קשה להר"ם מהך דמעביר עציץ נקוב בכרם: אם הוסיף מאתים — אסור, לא הוסיף מאתים — מותר; אלמא דגידולי איסור אינם אוסרים במשהו! וכן מצינו בהך ד"בצלים שירדו עליהם גשמים וצמחו, הוריקו — מותרין"; אלמא דגידולי שביעית אינם אוסרים במשהו. לכך מפרש הר"ם דהכא מיירי בבצל שנעקר בששית ונטעה בשביעית, ומכיון שהוסיף משהו נאסר כולו, כמו כלאי הכרם דעיקרם נאסר; דה"נ אמר התם: זרעו מעיקרו בהשרשה — כלומר כשתחלת זריעתו באיסור נאסר בהשרשה, אבל זרוע ובא — הוסיף אין, לא הוסיף לא; והכי נמי תחלת זריעתו באיסור היתה. מיהו יש ליישב ד"לביעור" קשה, דהיה לו לומר "לגידולין"; אין לו זריעה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:2:2.english: He said to them: Sabbatical-Year [produce] does not prohibit in any amount except with regard to the removal of produce - Rabbi Eliezer explained: For example, sixth-year produce that entered the Sabbatical Year and grew slightly, and [therefore] requires removal like Sabbatical-Year produce, because forbidden growths are considered significant and nullify the permitted principal. However, with regard to eating — for example, after the time of removal, with Sabbatical-Year produce that became mixed with permitted produce — it does not prohibit in any amount, but rather by imparting flavor, like other forbidden items. Thus, Sabbatical-Year growths nullify a permitted principal; so too, let us say in our dilemma regarding the onion that permitted growths nullify a forbidden principal. And [the Gemara] rejects [this]: Here too we follow the stringency, [namely] that Sabbatical-Year growths nullify the [permitted] principal, but to be lenient, permitted growths do not nullify a forbidden principal. And regarding what he explained, "except with regard to removal," as referring to sixth-year produce that enters the Sabbatical Year, this is difficult for the Ram: for it is taught [in a baraita], "All aftergrowths are permitted except for aftergrowths of cabbage," and we explain that it is speaking of sixth-year aftergrowths that enter the Sabbatical Year — thus, Sabbatical-Year growths do not prohibit in any amount! And it appears [one can answer] that perhaps there it is speaking of [produce] that finished growing in the sixth year and did not grow at all in the Sabbatical Year, and aftergrowths of cabbage are forbidden as [the Gemara] explains: lest one take from the [new] leaves and say, "I took from the original stalks." And furthermore, it is difficult for the Ram from that [mishna] of one who carries a perforated pot through a vineyard: if it increased by a two-hundredth [part], it is forbidden; if it did not increase by a two-hundredth [part], it is permitted — thus, forbidden growths do not prohibit in any amount! And similarly we find in that [mishna] of "onions upon which rain fell and they sprouted... [if] they turned green, they are permitted" — thus, Sabbatical-Year growths do not prohibit in any amount. Therefore, the Ram explains that here it is speaking of an onion that was uprooted in the sixth year and planted in the Sabbatical Year, and once it increased slightly, the entire [onion] becomes forbidden, like forbidden food crops in a vineyard whose principal becomes forbidden; for so too [the Gemara] states there: "If he planted it from the beginning, [it is forbidden] upon taking root" — that is to say, when its initial planting is in a forbidden state [it becomes forbidden upon taking root], [whereas if] it was already planted and continued growing — if it increased [by a two-hundredth], yes [it is forbidden]; if it did not increase, no [it is permitted]; and here too its initial planting was in a forbidden state. However, this requires reconciliation, for [the word] "for removal" is difficult, as he should have said "for growths"; it has no sowing.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:4:1.english: Onions - Of the eve of the Sabbatical year [i.e., the sixth year].

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:4:2.english: And rain fell upon them - [during] the Sabbatical year, and they sprouted.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:4:3.english: If their leaves are black - For it is their nature to turn black [i.e., dark green] when rain falls upon them.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:4:4.english: Forbidden - For it is certain that most of them grew in the Sabbatical [year].

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:4:5.english: They turned green - Their majority did not grow, and [therefore] they are permitted.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:5:1.hebrew: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס אומר - אף בשלא הושחרו, אם יכולין וכו' שגדלו כל כך — אסורין, דבידוע שגדלו רובם בשביעית:
Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:5:1.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says - Even when [their leaves] have not turned black, "if they can [be uprooted by their leaves], etc." — [meaning] that they have grown so much — they are forbidden, for it is known that most of them grew during the Sabbatical year.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:5:2.hebrew: וכנגדם למוצאי שביעית מותרין - כלומר: בצלים שבאים משביעית לשמינית, אלמא דגידולי היתר מבטלין לאיסור:
Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:5:2.english: And in the parallel [situation], at the conclusion of the Sabbatical Year they are permitted - That is to say, onions that come from the Sabbatical Year into the eighth [year]; thus [it is evident] that permitted growth neutralizes the prohibition.

Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:5:3.hebrew: ודלמא במדוכנים - שדכו אותם במדוכה בשביעית ולא חשיבי, ובטלים בגידולין; אבל היכא דלא דכו, מיבעיא לן אי בטלו אי לא בטלו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 58a:5:3.english: And perhaps with regard to crushed [onions] - [Meaning] that they pounded them in a mortar during the Sabbatical Year and they are not significant, and [thus] they are nullified by the [permitted] growth; but where they did not pound [them], it is a question for us whether they are nullified or whether they are not nullified.
